problem: Prior VLN data augmentation relies on limited simulator scenes and predefined templates/rules for instructions (e.g., Lily on YouTube-VLN), giving fixed-format instructions that are poorly aligned with visual observations and trajectories.
motivation: VLN agents overfit to seen environments due to scarce realistic scenes and high-quality path-instruction pairs. YouTube house tours are abundant and realistic, and large multimodal models can understand images and generate flexible text, but they hallucinate, so generation needs grounding and verification.
key_idea: Use ChatGPT-4V, fed trajectories sampled from YouTube house tours with CLIP node labels and inverse-model actions, to generate multi-granularity instructions, filtered by a consistency and regex verification mechanism, then pre-train a ViLBERT-like agent on the pairs.
insight: Grounding the LMM with explicit node labels and actions and re-extracting (node, action) pairs to check them against the ground-truth trajectory cuts hallucinations. The ablation on R2R val-unseen shows SR rising from 67.42 (no verification) to 69.32 (consistency) to 70.9 (plus regex), close to 71.10 with manual review. Mixing R2R and rewritten instructions (R2R*) helps further, indicating that instruction richness aids generalization.
method: Trajectory sampling: sample room and transition node trajectories from 3879 YouTube house-tour videos following Lily.
Node labeling: CLIP annotates each room node with room type and key objects ('Object with Room') to reduce LMM visual hallucination.
Action grounding: an action inverse model estimates the actions between room nodes, giving (image, label, action) triplets, with the last action set to Stop.
Instruction generation: prompt ChatGPT-4V with the triplets and an output-format example, forbidding extra visual description, with granularity (concise/detailed) controlled by the prompt.

Verification mechanism: a consistency module extracts (node label, action) pairs from the generated instruction and compares them with the ground truth, regenerating on mismatch; regex rules remove special characters and prompt leakage.
Trajectory judgment / pre-training: a ViLBERT-like model is trained with MLM, MVM, Path-Instruction Judgment (negatives from shuffled node order) and Path Ranking.
Fine-tuning: fine-tune on R2R, R2R# (R2R trajectories rewritten by InstruGen) or R2R* (mix of both).

results: On R2R the method reaches SR 81.23 (val-seen) and 71.10 (val-unseen), beating Lily (79.31 / 70.00) and Airbert (73.85 / 68.67). It also gets 29.35 SR in zero-shot RxR val-unseen versus Lily 27.20, and 51.25 SR in the one-shot val-unseen setting versus Lily 50.86.
limitations: Samples discrete R2R-like trajectories, which may not transfer to continuous navigation.
Depends on the proprietary ChatGPT-4V and on CLIP/inverse-model label quality; the gains over Lily are small (about 1 SR point on val-unseen).
Evaluated only on R2R and RxR, with no comparison against stronger recent agents.
